purpose: Research source audit, not presentation slides or a course-report draft.

sources.title: When Does Generating More Help?
verified_facts: The baseline samples until 32 correct responses per question; smaller r uses the first r.
Source expansion versus response sampling is compared within equal q*r example-count buckets.
Students use equal epochs; repeated configurations have three training seeds.
In Mathematics, larger question pools match smaller pools at low budget and outperform at higher budget.
sources.implication: Our small-budget non-difference does not refute this paper. Equal accepted inventory is distinct from finite acquisition cost including failed attempts.

sources.title: OpenMathInstruct-2
verified_facts: 256K pairs are held fixed while unique questions range from 1K to 6.5K.
The MATH validation result improves with greater question count.
sources.implication: Direct P/R precedent at much larger average R; not a universal R=1 recommendation.

sources.title: X-Coder
verified_facts: The paper reports an advantage for greater task count.
The paper does discuss verification and data-construction costs.
sources.implication: Low-R allocation is already studied; do not claim cost was entirely omitted or generalize our GSM8K result to code.

sources.title: DART-Math
verified_facts: Difficulty-aware generation and one-response coverage are explicit prior work.
Its synthesis-cost analysis varies maximum raw attempts and reports unmet response quotas.
It explicitly discusses potentially trading coverage attainment against generation cost.
sources.implication: Failed-attempt and difficult-parent costs are not new observations by themselves; purchasing new parents is a separate intervention.

sources.title: Data Repetition Beats Data Scaling in Long-CoT SFT
verified_facts: The experimental budget is optimizer updates, with batch size one.
The grid varies unique examples and repetition epochs, with independent runs and full warmup schedules.
Termination is reported with accuracy and pass rate.
sources.implication: Retain exact replay and termination diagnostics. Our same-parent extra-answer result is not a direct replication of its long-CoT setting.

sources.title: Generalization in LLM Problem Solving: The Case of the Shortest Path
verified_facts: Question/answer allocation is studied under fixed numbers of training records.
More distinct start/end pairs improve transfer on disjoint maps in the reported setup.
sources.implication: The general problem is not new; the controlled graph result need not dictate a low-dose pretrained math result.

novelty_status: No claim of exhaustive coverage or established novelty. A new empirical contribution requires a validated acquisition decision beyond re-running P/R grids.
